visa-preparation.fastest_entry: Australian citizens need no visa or NZeTA, unless they have a criminal record or have been deported from any country.
visa-preparation.before_departure: New Zealand Traveller Declaration (NZTD), free, online or in the app, before passport control.

steps.step: Complete the free NZTD before arrival.

steps: With a conviction or past deportation, contact a New Zealand Visa Application Centre well before travel.

baseline_unverified.host_unlock: No immigration sponsor is required. A host adds value by documenting the invitation, role, dates, venue, fee or expenses, tax classification and any professional or event permissions.
baseline_unverified.before_departure: Travel on the Australian passport. Complete the free New Zealand Traveller Declaration from 24 hours before the journey begins. If character eligibility is uncertain, resolve it with Immigration New Zealand before flying.
baseline_unverified.useful_stay: The resident visa permits an indefinite stay. It expires on departure unless travel conditions have been varied; this usually does not prevent a qualifying Australian citizen receiving a fresh resident visa on a later arrival.
baseline_unverified.from: Luke's earlier precursor notes; not verified against an official source and not an authority. Kept because no official page covers this point yet.

culture-and-protocol.welcome_and_acknowledgement: The Tiaki Promise (tiaki means to care for and protect in te reo Māori) asks visitors to care for land, sea and nature by treading lightly and leaving no trace; to travel safely and with consideration for others; and to respect culture and local communities with an open heart and mind.
culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Leave no trace; travel safely and considerately; respect Māori culture and local communities.
culture-and-protocol.cultural_authority: Mana whenua (local iwi) for their own places; the Tiaki Promise as the national visitor commitment.
culture-and-protocol.note: From the country's own government or national tourism body.

items.text: The CAA publishes a list of Part 102 unmanned aircraft operator certificate holders.

A Part 102 certificate is needed to fly outside the Part 101 rules (for example over people or property without consent, or aircraft over 25 kg). A Part 141 training qualification is not a Part 102 certificate.
Not yet checked: whether a foreign visitor may fly commercially under Part 101; Part 102 applications need an address for service in New Zealand (Part 102.9).
Tourism New Zealand's Visual Library (registration, some assets need approval) and Media library (royalty-free editorial and broadcast visuals, including b-roll).
